items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: Well, Piggly Wiggly, was that your first record with Johnny Dodds? That was my first recording in Chicago.

ctx.x: Oralman Half Pats was formed around 1937, 1936 I think. When I first went to Chicago, it was in 29, and then I was on the side. That's where I recorded the Melrose Brothers. That's when I made Piggler Wiggler and called them title. I think it's on a Paramount record. A vocal, no, a vocalian. And then I left and went up in Michigan playing with Frank Terrace Band and came back to New Orleans. So the Oralman Half Pats was formed after I went back later in 1937. 1936, 37.

Well, Piggly Wiggly, was that your first record with Johnny Dodds? That was my first recording in Chicago. That's... Now, do you remember any of the other tunes that you wrote back around that time? You said you did Old Red. Yeah, we did Old Red and then we did a Dliper song. You wrote that yourself?

No, I just... I didn't write it. Just one of those things, a song you used to sing around Chicago. I really don't know who really wrote it, but I put most of the music to it. I just played my idea of the music, to feel a vibe. I really don't know who the song belongs to, to tell you the truth.
